intro: If you're road-tripping through Uthai Thani and want a spotless, modern room with a comfortable bed and free parking right outside — without paying much — C2U Hotel Uthai Thani is a name self-drivers in this area mention often. It's a newer 3-star, three-storey hotel with around 36 rooms, set just outside town on the bypass road (Highway 333) in Nong Khayang, about 5 km from the centre of Uthai Thani. Modern air-con rooms with flat-screen TVs, fridges and free bottled water, plus free parking, free Wi-Fi, an on-site mini-mart and breakfast. Rates start from approx. ฿800/night.

body.html: What guests talk about most at C2U Hotel is the clean, modern rooms that feel a notch above the price. This is a newer build, so everything still looks fresh, and a lot of real reviews say the same things: the room is spotless, the bed is comfy, the linens are good quality, and the power outlets and light switches around the bed are thoughtfully placed. It's a stay for people who value a good night's sleep in a clean room over a central location or resort-style facilities.

The location is the one thing to understand before you book — the hotel sits outside town on the bypass road (Highway 333) in Nong Khayang, about 5 km from the centre of Uthai Thani. It's roughly a 10-minute drive into town for the morning market, the Sakae Krang River and Wat Ubosatharam, and an easy run out to Wat Chantharam (Tha Sung) with its famous glass temple. The upside of a roadside spot is easy access in and out and plenty of parking, which makes it a sensible base for a self-drive trip around the province.

Rooms are air-conditioned and styled in a clean, modern way, with flat-screen TVs, fridges, free bottled water and walk-in showers stocked with toiletries. Guests praise the cleanliness and the practical, well-thought-out design — lighting, sockets and storage all in sensible places. Wi-Fi is free throughout, there's a 24-hour front desk and round-the-clock security (handy for late arrivals), and a small on-site mini-mart for essentials.
"Very clean room, comfortable bed, new appliances, well-placed power outlets. The hotel is new and modern, staff are helpful, breakfast was good — great value, just a bit far from town."

Breakfast is a continental spread that several reviews describe as nicely done, served in a pleasant little dining area. The detail self-drivers love most is the large, free car park right out front — no jostling for a space. And because it's on the bypass, getting in and out to reach sights around Uthai Thani is smoother than from the narrow streets of an in-town stay.

To be straight with you, the main trade-off here is the out-of-town location with nothing within walking distance. Almost every critical review says the same thing: it's far from the centre, and once you step out there are no restaurants or shops to walk to, so you'll drive into town for every meal. Without your own vehicle it's awkward. There's also no swimming pool and no restaurant for meals other than breakfast. One more thing worth checking: at times the hotel takes cash only, so bring cash to be safe.

Overall, C2U Hotel scores around 8.1 out of 10 across booking platforms, from 800-plus real reviews, with cleanliness rated very highly. It isn't an in-town stay you can wander out from, and there's no pool or full restaurant — but measured on clean, modern rooms, a good bed, a big free car park, decent breakfast and a starting rate around ฿800 (rising in peak periods), it's a really sensible pick for self-drive travellers who want a good room on a friendly budget.

A tip from reading the reviews: this place is built for travellers with a car. Plan to have lunch and dinner in central Uthai Thani, since there's nothing around the hotel. Carry some cash, and if you're arriving late, the 24-hour front desk has you covered. Use it as a comfortable base, then drive into town for boat noodles, the morning market, and an early boat trip to watch the fish along the Sakae Krang River — that's Uthai Thani at its best.

faq.q: Where is C2U Hotel Uthai Thani · is it far from town?
faq.a: C2U Hotel is at 88 Moo 1, Nong Khayang, Mueang Uthai Thani, on the bypass road (Highway 333). It's outside the centre, about 5 km away — roughly a 10-minute drive into town for the market, the Sakae Krang River and Wat Ubosatharam. It suits travellers with their own car best.

faq.q: How much is C2U Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿800/night for a Standard room. There are Standard, Deluxe and Twin/Triple rooms for groups — all air-conditioned with flat-screen TVs, fridges and free bottled water. Prices rise in peak periods, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does C2U Hotel have parking and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's a large free car park ideal for self-drivers, and a continental breakfast that reviews describe as nicely done. There's also a small on-site mini-mart for essentials and a 24-hour front desk.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at C2U Hotel · are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are air-conditioned and styled in a clean, modern way, with flat-screen TVs, fridges, free bottled water and walk-in showers. Real reviews particularly praise the cleanliness and comfortable beds, noting good-quality linens and thoughtfully placed power outlets and switches around the bed.

faq.q: Does C2U Hotel have a swimming pool or restaurant?
faq.a: No — there's no swimming pool and no restaurant for meals other than breakfast. Because it's out of town with nothing nearby, you'll drive into central Uthai Thani for lunch and dinner, about a 10-minute drive away.

faq.q: Who is C2U Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for self-drive travellers who want a clean, modern room with a good bed and easy parking on a friendly budget — couples, families or anyone using Uthai Thani as a stopover or a base for driving around the province. It's not a good fit for car-free travellers who want to walk to sights and food in town.
